title: I2S audio port with an AXI4 DMA: one stereo frame per 32-bit word, TX and RX, underrun / overrun counters
features: The unchanged I2S_top core (16-bit Philips I2S slave) fed and drained by the shared AXI4 engine.
One word per stereo frame: bits 15:0 left, bits 31:16 right.
TX: word k plays in the frame after the one in which it was taken; with no word ready a frame repeats the previous one (TX_UNDERRUN).
RX: one word per frame received entirely after START; a word not taken by the engine in time is replaced by the next frame (RX_OVERRUN).
FRAMES counts the frames played (TX jobs) or received (RX-only jobs).

fields.desc: frames (32-bit words); 0: the job ends at once
start a job (TX_EN or RX_EN set); ignored while busy
the current / last job saw an AXI error response (cleared by start)
frames played / received by the current / last job
TX frames repeated for want of data
RX frames lost (replaced by a newer one)
clocks from start to DONE of the current / last job

irqs.name: ERR
irqs.desc: a job ended that saw an AXI error response

sequence: Write SRC_ADDR / DST_ADDR (word aligned) and LEN (frames).
Wait for irq, read FRAMES and XRUN, write 1s to IRQ_STATUS to clear it.
notes: bclk, lrck, sdin and sdout are the I2S pins (slave: the codec drives BCLK and LRCK); they pass through unchanged. Each BCLK phase must last at least three clocks.

m_* is the AXI4 manager port (32-bit address and data, 4-bit ID, no user / QoS); it passes through unchanged. Bursts are INCR, AxSIZE = 2 (4 bytes), 1 to 16 beats, WSTRB = 4'hF, never across a 4 KB boundary; one read and one write burst are outstanding at a time. A read burst is issued only when its data has room, a write burst only when all its data is ready.
